text: I have a capacity in my soul for taking in God entirely. I am as sure as I live that nothing is so near to me as God. God is nearer to me than I am to myself; my existence depends on the nearness and presence of God.
note: feeling far from God; the divine is nearest of all

tags.when_helps: A believer feeling far from God or alone, who needs reminding that the divine is closer than their own self.

display_text: I have a capacity in my soul for taking in God entirely. I am as sure as I live that nothing is so near to me as God. God is nearer to me than I am to myself; my existence depends on the nearness and presence of God.
plain: My soul has room to take in God completely. I am certain that nothing is as near to me as God. God is nearer to me than I am to myself, and my existence depends on his presence.
core_idea: God is nearer to me than I am to myself

text: To serve God with fear is good; to serve Him out of love is better; but to fear and love Him together is best of all. To have a restful or peaceful life in God is good; to bear a life of pain in patience is better; but to have peace in the midst of pain is the best of all.
note: finding peace in the midst of pain

keywords: peace in the midst of pain
tags.when_helps: A person of faith living with ongoing pain who wants to find peace within it rather than waiting for it to end.

display_text: To serve God with fear is good; to serve Him out of love is better; but to fear and love Him together is best of all. To have a restful or peaceful life in God is good; to bear a life of pain in patience is better; but to have peace in the midst of pain is the best of all.
plain: Serving God from fear is good, from love better, from fear and love together best. A peaceful life in God is good, bearing pain patiently better, but peace in the middle of pain is best of all.
core_idea: Best of all is peace in the midst of pain

text: A man may go into the field and say his prayer and be aware of God, or, he may be in Church and be aware of God; but, if he is more aware of Him because he is in a quiet place, that is his own deficiency and not due to God, Who is alike present in all things and places, and is willing to give Himself everywhere so far as lies in Him. He knows God rightly who knows Him everywhere.
note: finding the sacred everywhere, not only in quiet places

tags.when_helps: Someone who can only feel God in quiet places and wants to sense the sacred in ordinary, busy life.

display_text: A man may go into the field and say his prayer and be aware of God, or, he may be in Church and be aware of God; but, if he is more aware of Him because he is in a quiet place, that is his own deficiency and not due to God, Who is alike present in all things and places, and is willing to give Himself everywhere so far as lies in Him. He knows God rightly who knows Him everywhere.
plain: You can be aware of God praying in a field or in church. If you feel him more in a quiet place, that is your shortcoming, not God's, for he is present everywhere. Whoever knows God everywhere knows him rightly.
core_idea: Knowing God rightly means finding him everywhere

text: No man desires anything so eagerly as God desires to bring men to the knowledge of Himself. God is always ready, but we are very unready. God is near us, but we are far from Him. God is within, and we are without. God is friendly; we are estranged.
note: feeling estranged from God; the distance is ours

keywords: God is friendly; we are estranged
tags.when_helps: A believer who feels estranged from God and wonders whether God is willing to come near.

display_text: No man desires anything so eagerly as God desires to bring men to the knowledge of Himself. God is always ready, but we are very unready. God is near us, but we are far from Him. God is within, and we are without. God is friendly; we are estranged.
plain: No one wants anything as eagerly as God wants people to know him. God is always ready; we are not. God is near, we are far; God is within, we are without; God is friendly, we are estranged.
core_idea: God is always near; we are the ones far away

text: There were a certain man and wife; the woman by accident lost an eye, and was sorely troubled thereat. Her husband then said to her, "Wife, why are you troubled? "She answered, "It is not the loss of my eye that troubles me, but the thought that you may love me less on account of that loss." He said, "I love you all the same." Not long after he put one of his own eyes out, and came to his wife and said, "Wife, that you may believe I love you, I have made myself like you: I, too, now, have only one eye." So men could hardly believe that God loved them till God put one of His eyes out, that is took upon Himself human nature, and was made man.
note: fear of being unlovable after loss; love that shares it

tags.when_helps: Someone who fears being loved less after a loss or change to their body, or who doubts God's love.

display_fix: Misplaced space around closing quotation mark
plain: A wife who lost an eye feared her husband would love her less, so he put out one of his own to show his love. Likewise, people could hardly believe God loved them until God took on human nature.
core_idea: God became human to show his love

text: If the earth flee downward from heaven, it finds heaven beneath it; if it flee upward, it comes again to heaven. The earth cannot flee from heaven: whether it flee up or down, the heaven rains its influence upon it, and stamps its impress upon it, and makes it fruitful, whether it be willing or not. Thus doth God with men: whoever thinketh to escape Him, flies into His bosom, for every corner is open to Him.
note: running from God or grace; no escape from love

tags.when_helps: A believer who has been running from God and fears there is no way back.

display_text: If the earth flee downward from heaven, it finds heaven beneath it; if it flee upward, it comes again to heaven. The earth cannot flee from heaven: whether it flee up or down, the heaven rains its influence upon it, and stamps its impress upon it, and makes it fruitful, whether it be willing or not. Thus doth God with men: whoever thinketh to escape Him, flies into His bosom, for every corner is open to Him.
plain: Whichever way the earth flees from heaven, it meets heaven, which makes it fruitful whether it wants this or not. So God does with people: whoever tries to escape him flies into his arms; every corner is open to him.
core_idea: No one can escape God; fleeing leads to him

text: Whoso will hear the wisdom of the Father must dwell deep, and abide at home, and be at unity with himself. Three things hinder us from hearing the everlasting Word. The first is fleshliness, the second is distraction, the third is the illusion of time. If a man could get free of these, he would dwell in eternity, and in the spirit, and in solitude, and in the desert, and there would hear the everlasting Word.
note: distraction and inner unity in spiritual listening

tags.when_helps: Someone distracted and scattered who wants to understand what keeps them from inner listening.

display_text: Whoso will hear the wisdom of the Father must dwell deep, and abide at home, and be at unity with himself. Three things hinder us from hearing the everlasting Word. The first is fleshliness, the second is distraction, the third is the illusion of time. If a man could get free of these, he would dwell in eternity, and in the spirit, and in solitude, and in the desert, and there would hear the everlasting Word.
plain: To hear the Father's wisdom you must live deep within, at home and at one with yourself. Bodily appetite, distraction and the illusion of time block the eternal Word; free of them, you would hear it.
core_idea: Inner unity frees us to hear God's eternal Word

plain_judge.issue: Drops dwelling in eternity, spirit, solitude and desert as the outcome.

text: If thou really lovest thyself, thou lovest all men as thyself; as long as thou lovest any one less than thyself, thou dost not really love thyself. That man is right who loves all men as himself. Some folk say: "I love my friends, who do me kindness, more than other people." Such love is imperfect and incomplete; it is like having your sails only half-filled with wind. When I love anyone as much as myself, I would just as soon that joy or sorrow, death or life were mine, as well as his. That would be the dictate of right reason.

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone whose love stops at friends and kin, and who is asked to widen it to everyone.

display_text: If thou really lovest thyself, thou lovest all men as thyself; as long as thou lovest any one less than thyself, thou dost not really love thyself. That man is right who loves all men as himself. Some folk say: "I love my friends, who do me kindness, more than other people." Such love is imperfect and incomplete; it is like having your sails only half-filled with wind. When I love anyone as much as myself, I would just as soon that joy or sorrow, death or life were mine, as well as his. That would be the dictate of right reason.
plain: If you truly love yourself, you love everyone as yourself; loving anyone less means you don't really love yourself. Loving only friends who are kind to you is a half-filled sail.
core_idea: True self-love means loving everyone equally

plain_judge.issue: Drops the closing ideal of sharing another's joy, sorrow, life and death as one's own.

text: If my eye is to discern colour, it must itself be free from all colour. The eye with which I see God is the same with which God sees me. My eye and God's eye is one eye, and one sight, and one knowledge, and one love.
note: union with God; seeing and being seen

tags.when_helps: A contemplative seeker drawn to the idea of union with God and wanting to dwell on it.

display_text: If my eye is to discern colour, it must itself be free from all colour. The eye with which I see God is the same with which God sees me. My eye and God's eye is one eye, and one sight, and one knowledge, and one love.
plain: To see colour the eye must have none itself. The eye that sees God is the same eye through which God sees me; God's sight and mine are one.
core_idea: God's seeing and mine are one sight

plain_judge.issue: Drops 'one knowledge, and one love'; unity reduced to sight alone.

text: And supposing a man had renounced himself for twenty years, if he took himself back for a moment, that man's renunciation would be as nothing. The man who has truly renounced himself and does not once cast a glance on what he has renounced, and thus remains immovable and unalterable, that man alone has really renounced self.
note: letting go fully without looking back

tags.when_helps: Someone on a spiritual path tempted to take back what they gave up, who needs a firm reminder.

display_text: And supposing a man had renounced himself for twenty years, if he took himself back for a moment, that man's renunciation would be as nothing. The man who has truly renounced himself and does not once cast a glance on what he has renounced, and thus remains immovable and unalterable, that man alone has really renounced self.
plain: Someone who gave up the self for twenty years but took it back for a moment would have given up nothing. Only one who never looks back at what was renounced has truly renounced the self.

text: Thou shouldest know that real sanctification consists in this that the spirit remain as immovable and unaffected by all impact of love or hate, joy or sorrow, honour or shame, as a huge mountain is unstirred by a gentle breeze. This immovable sanctification causes man to attain the nearest likeness to God that he is capable of.
note: equanimity amid praise, shame, joy and sorrow

tags.when_helps: Someone tossed between praise and blame, joy and sorrow, who longs for steady inner calm.

display_text: Thou shouldest know that real sanctification consists in this that the spirit remain as immovable and unaffected by all impact of love or hate, joy or sorrow, honour or shame, as a huge mountain is unstirred by a gentle breeze. This immovable sanctification causes man to attain the nearest likeness to God that he is capable of.
plain: Real holiness means the spirit stays unmoved by love or hate, joy or sorrow, honour or shame, like a mountain in a light breeze. This stillness brings a person as close to God's likeness as possible.
core_idea: Unshaken stillness of spirit makes us most like God

text: When God appears to be angry or to do us a kindness, it is we who are altered, while He remains unchangeable, as the same sunshine is injurious to weak eyes and beneficial to strong ones, remaining in itself the same.
note: feeling punished or favoured by God; the change is in us

tags.when_helps: A believer who feels God is angry with them and needs to see that God does not change.

display_text: When God appears to be angry or to do us a kindness, it is we who are altered, while He remains unchangeable, as the same sunshine is injurious to weak eyes and beneficial to strong ones, remaining in itself the same.
plain: When God seems angry or kind, it is we who change, not God, just as the same sunshine hurts weak eyes and helps strong ones.
core_idea: God stays the same; our state changes

text: If the heart is to be ready for the highest, it must he vacant of all other things. If I wish to write on a white tablet, whatever else is written on the tablet, however noble its purport, is a hindrance to me. If I am to write, I must wipe the tablet clean of everything, and the tablet is most suitable for my purpose when it is blank. Similarly, if God is to write on my heart, everything else must come out of it till it is really sanctified. Only so can God work His highest will, and so the sanctified heart has no outward object at all.
note: emptying the heart to make room for the sacred

tags.when_helps: A seeker wanting to make room for God by clearing out other attachments of the heart.

display_text: If the heart is to be ready for the highest, it must he vacant of all other things. plain: A heart ready for the highest must be empty of everything else, like a blank tablet. If God is to write on your heart, all else must be cleared out first.
core_idea: God can write only on an emptied heart

plain_judge.issue: Drops 'however noble' and that the sanctified heart has no outward object.

text: The quickest means to bring us to perfection is suffering; none enjoy everlasting blessedness more than those who share with Christ the bitterest pangs. Nothing is sharper than suffering, nothing is sweeter than to have suffered. The surest foundation in which this perfection may rest is humility; whatever here crawls in the deepest abjectness, that the Spirit lifts to the very heights of God, for love brings suffering and suffering brings love.
note: suffering as a path to growth and love

tags.when_helps: A Christian enduring suffering who wants to find meaning and closeness to Christ within it.

display_text: The quickest means to bring us to perfection is suffering; none enjoy everlasting blessedness more than those who share with Christ the bitterest pangs. Nothing is sharper than suffering, nothing is sweeter than to have suffered. The surest foundation in which this perfection may rest is humility; whatever here crawls in the deepest abjectness, that the Spirit lifts to the very heights of God, for love brings suffering and suffering brings love.
plain: Suffering is the fastest way to perfection, and those who share Christ's sharpest pain enjoy the greatest blessedness. Humility is its foundation, for love brings suffering and suffering brings love.
core_idea: Suffering and humility lead to perfection through love

plain_judge.issue: Drops 'nothing sweeter than to have suffered' and the lowly being lifted to God.

text: Fire converts wood into its own likeness, and the stronger the wind blows, the greater grows the fire. Now by the fire understand love, and by the wind the Holy Spirit. The stronger the influence of the Holy Spirit, the brighter grows the fire of love; but not all at once, rather gradually as the soul grows.
note: Spiritual growth is gradual; love grows slowly

tags.when_helps: A believer impatient with slow spiritual growth, reassured that love grows gradually.

display_text: Fire converts wood into its own likeness, and the stronger the wind blows, the greater grows the fire. Now by the fire understand love, and by the wind the Holy Spirit. The stronger the influence of the Holy Spirit, the brighter grows the fire of love; but not all at once, rather gradually as the soul grows.
plain: As wind makes fire grow, so the Holy Spirit makes the fire of love grow brighter in the soul, not all at once but gradually as the soul grows.
core_idea: The Holy Spirit gradually brightens the soul's love

text: There never was a Saint so great as to be immovable. I can never arrive at a state when discord shall be as pleasing to my ears as harmony.
note: No one is beyond being shaken; accepting imperfection

tags.when_helps: Someone ashamed they are still shaken by discord, reassured that even saints are moved.

display_text: There never was a Saint so great as to be immovable. I can never arrive at a state when discord shall be as pleasing to my ears as harmony.
plain: No saint was ever so great as to be completely unmoved. I can never reach a point where discord pleases me as much as harmony.
core_idea: Even saints are not wholly unmoved

text: The essence of morality is inwardness, the intensity of will from which it springs, and the nobleness of the aim for which it is practiced. When a good work is done by a man, he is free of it, and through that freedom is liker and nearer to his Original than he was before.
note: Goodness comes from intention; doing good frees you

tags.when_helps: Someone wondering whether their good deeds count, who wants to understand what makes an act truly good.

display_text: The essence of morality is inwardness, the intensity of will from which it springs, and the nobleness of the aim for which it is practiced. When a good work is done by a man, he is free of it, and through that freedom is liker and nearer to his Original than he was before.
plain: What makes an act moral is its inner source: the strength of will behind it and the nobility of its aim. Doing good frees a person and brings them nearer to their divine origin.
core_idea: Morality lies in inner will and noble aim

text: All grief except grief for sin comes from love of the world. In God is neither sorrow, nor grief, nor trouble. Wouldst thou be free from all grief and trouble, abide and walk in God, and to God alone. As long as love of the creature is in us, pain cannot cease.
note: Grief rooted in attachment; finding rest beyond it

tags.when_helps: A devout reader asking why their sorrow persists, who is open to a hard teaching on attachment.

display_text: All grief except grief for sin comes from love of the world. In God is neither sorrow, nor grief, nor trouble. Wouldst thou be free from all grief and trouble, abide and walk in God, and to God alone. As long as love of the creature is in us, pain cannot cease.
plain: All grief except grief for sin comes from loving the world. God holds no sorrow, so abide in God alone to be free of it; while we love created things, pain continues.
core_idea: Grief comes from attachment to the world

text: If thou sufferest only regarding thyself, from whatever cause it may be, that suffering causes grief to thee, and is hard to bear. But if thou sufferest regarding God and Him alone, that suffering is not grievous, nor hard to bear, because God bears the load.
note: Suffering eased when not borne alone

situations: caring for a sick or ageing relative
tags.when_helps: A person of faith crushed by suffering who needs to hear they need not carry it alone.

display_text: If thou sufferest only regarding thyself, from whatever cause it may be, that suffering causes grief to thee, and is hard to bear. But if thou sufferest regarding God and Him alone, that suffering is not grievous, nor hard to bear, because God bears the load.
plain: Suffering endured only for yourself is grievous and hard to bear. Suffering endured for God alone is not heavy, because God carries the load.
core_idea: Suffering borne for God is lightened by God
